I am an old woman here in Mulanje, and this small plot near the house is where I grow sorghum together with pigeon peas and some pumpkins. I have no money for chemical fertilizer this year — the price at the ADMARC is too much for me — so I will use the manure from my goats and chickens like my mother taught me. The seed I keep from last year's harvest, it knows our soil and the rains. My daughters and I will work the plot ourselves; the rains come from the sky, not from any pump.
